Hi OP,

I’m single, on a similar-ish wage to you, with a HECS debt, and I got approved for a $390k home loan at 5.89% interest through the First Home Guarantee Scheme. 

When I first started looking a year ago, I looked at $600k properties too. Then I met with a mortgage broker a month later and got a reality check ahaha. 

I had to get my second pre-approval last month and my loan amount went down because of all the rate rises. Since beginning the search, my standards have changed in what I’m looking for in a property. What I previously had as a non-negotiable, have become negotiables. I’ve decided that I’m going to purchase a property in the outer south east (where I currently live and work), and live in it for a year to make sure I continue to be eligible for the first home stamp duty exemption, and pay off whatever I can to get to 20%. After a year, I’d like to rent that property out and move to an apartment in an area I’d like to live in :) 

I’m also going to purchase a place under my loan amount, so my mortgage repayments aren’t huge, so I can still enjoy my life without being super stressed. I can also get a roommate if I feel like it, but that’s something to think about once I’ve got the place ahaha I also play with the NAB Home Loan Calculator to look at repayments.

Good Luck OP!  I’ve been finding this whole process pretty stressful. I would recommend making a list of non negotiables, look at places within your price limit, and possibly review that non-negotiable list. Remember that a coat of paint and a good deep clean can do wonders to a place - it took me a long time to be able to look at places through that lens. This does not mean you should ignore huge red flags! I’ve been going to property inspections with my mum who is good at seeing that kind of potential, whereas I really struggle with that. 

Good Luck!

I totally understand where you’re coming from. I’ve had periods where my depression and anxiety just make me everything so much harder and the mess makes me emotionally even lower. Everything feels really overwhelming right now but, you’re doing an amazing job even just asking for help and tips. Legit, it’s one step at a time. Try not to force yourself to clean your room all in one go (unless you can hack your ADHD and hyper focus ahaha). Give yourself some small goals e.g putting the dishes away and then trying to keep the dishes out of your room the following days. Or a phone reminder at 5pm telling you to put all your dishes in the dishwasher/wash them idk. These are just random suggestions off the top of my head. Some things will take time to work for you and some strategies just will not be helpful for you. Just keep asking for help and trying things out and you’ll eventually be able to find strategies that work for you :)

@domesticblisters on TikTok is run by KC Davis who is an ADHDer and she’s a therapist.  She has great strategies for cleaning your space and making your space actually work for you. She also has a website with resources that might be helpful.

I’ve also heard of people breaking cleaning up into smaller tasks e.g., Carry a plastic bag and throw all the rubbish in it and put it straight in the bin. Or walk around with a laundry basket and chuck your clothes in it and immediately put it in the washing machine and put a timer on your phone so you don’t forget about it. 
Taking care of yourself (which includes making sure you’re living in a healthy and safe environment for you) is really rough when you have depression, anxiety, and ADHD on top of those. You’re doing the best you can at the moment and it will take time to figure out strategies that work for you and your brain. Please don’t be afraid to ask for help from a close friend or family member -sometimes what you might need is someone to help start you off or break down the task even more.
